title: Over-Receipt Carry-Forward on FBN Inbound-Shortage Claims
content:
**Clause.** On a Fulfilled by Northloop (FBN) inbound-shortage claim, the over-receipt carry-forward is the excess of units received over units expected on the SKU's other inbound lines dated inside the carry span, taken together and counted only when that excess is positive; the carry span is the long carry span of 12 months for an enrollment in FBN Scale Program, FBN Premier Program or FBN Enterprise Program active at least the carry tenure of 24 whole months since its activation date, the middle carry span of 6 months for an enrollment in FBN Core Program or FBN Growth Program active at least that carry tenure of 24 whole months, and zero months for every other enrollment.

For the over-receipt carry-forward, a receipt is dated inside the carry span when fewer than the carry span's number of whole months have passed from its receipt date to the handling date, a whole month passing on the same day number of a later month, and a carry span of zero months holds no receipt.

## Carry span

| Enrollment | Active 24 whole months or more | Carry span |
|---|---|---|
| FBN Scale, Premier or Enterprise Program | yes | 12 months |
| FBN Core or Growth Program | yes | 6 months |
| any program | no | 0 months: no receipt, no carry-forward |
| FBN Starter Program | any | 0 months: no receipt, no carry-forward |

## Example (hypothetical, FBN Core Program, active 30 whole months)

Other inbound lines of the same SKU received in the last 6 whole months: one received 104 against 100 expected, one received 48 against 50 expected. Taken together they show 152 received against 150 expected, an excess of 2: the carry-forward is 2 units. Had the second line received 44, the lines together would show 148 against 150; the excess is not positive and the carry-forward is 0. The claimed line itself is never one of the other lines.
